findings.problem: ShardWorkflow uses independent bool fields (is_validated, is_sent) and a String status, allowing illegal states such as is_sent=true with status="pending", both booleans false, or inconsistent lifecycle flags
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct or mutate ShardWorkflow into an invalid lifecycle state; invariants are checked at runtime rather than enforced by the type system
findings.fix: Replace is_validated and is_sent with a single ShardStatus enum typestate (e.g. Pending, Validated, Sent) that makes invalid transitions unconstructable

findings.problem: status field is pub String, a primitive type that allows any arbitrary string value (e.g. "sent", "SENT", "", "deleted") instead of a closed set of domain states
findings.failure_mode: callers can set status to any string, breaking downstream logic that assumes a small set of known states; no compile-time guarantee of valid status values
findings.fix: Replace String with a domain enum ShardStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } with #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]

findings.problem: mark_sent uses "sent".to_string() which allocates a heap String inside the functional core, and mutates the struct in place with (mut item) instead of returning a new state
findings.failure_mode: core logic is not pure—allocation introduces unpredictability, and in-place mutation makes the function harder to reason about, test, and compose; every call allocates a new String for the same constant
findings.fix: Return a new ShardWorkflow (or ShardStatus) with the enum variant instead of allocating; signature should be fn mark_sent(item: ShardWorkflow) -> ShardWorkflow using enum assignment

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is an independent flag separate from is_sent, allowing states like both false (unvalidated, unsent) and both true (validated, sent) without encoding the intended workflow ordering
findings.failure_mode: the lifecycle ordering (pending -> validated -> sent) is not enforced; callers can skip validation or re-mark as sent; no way to distinguish validated-but-not-yet-sent from other states
findings.fix: Consolidate into a single typestate enum with ordered variants that encode the workflow, making each state explicit and transitions explicit via fallible methods

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is independent of is_sent; sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some when is_sent=false, or None when is_sent=true, violating the invariant that sent-at time is present exactly when sent
findings.failure_mode: inconsistent data: a shard may appear sent without a timestamp (breaking audit) or have a timestamp without being marked sent (breaking dedup), requiring manual checks everywhere
findings.fix: Tie sent_at_epoch_ms into the typestate enum—e.g. Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } — so the timestamp is present by construction when in the Sent state

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership and mutates fields directly instead of using a pure functional pattern; the function has no input validation or guards on the current state before transitioning to sent
findings.failure_mode: any ShardWorkflow can be transitioned to sent regardless of its current state (e.g. already sent, never validated), allowing arbitrary state transitions that should be gated by the domain model
findings.fix: Add a fallible method or constructor that validates the current state (e.g. requires Validated) before producing Sent, returning a typed error on invalid transitions

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler data for allocation patterns in mark_sent
no allocation analysis (try_reserve or bounded capacity evidence)
no second-ring/command evidence for the domain workflow
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The crate represents illegal states fully, uses primitive types where domain enums are required, and allocates in the functional core. All violations are structural and would require a full refactor to resolve.
